subject: DPA: TOMs — cryptography, key custody & eSign logistics
messages:
From: Markus Lind <markus.lind@atlasfin.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@atlasfin.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA: TOMs — cryptography questions and signing plan

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for sending the TOMs exhibit draft. Our security and compliance team reviewed and has three principal questions before we send the DPA to Legal for final review:  

1) Key custody: can Redwood confirm which keys are customer-managed vs. Redwood-managed for Dedicated and Private deployments? We need explicit language on KMS responsibility, and whether HSM-backed keys are available.  

2) BYOK request: if we agree to a BYOK option, what is the operational handoff for key escrow, rotation cadence, and the rollback procedure?

3) Evidence for encryption in transit and at rest: sample S3 bucket policies, TLS ciphers accepted, and a statement on envelope signing workflow (DocuSign) and whether metadata leave EU regions during signing.

Would you be able to provide a short annex or supporting artifacts we can attach to the DPA? Also please advise who on your side will be executing the DocuSign envelope — we need a point of contact.

Regards,
Markus
Head of InfoSec, AtlasFin

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Markus Lind <markus.lind@atlasfin.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: TOMs — cryptography questions and signing plan

Hi Markus — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up top; I included Neha (security lead) and Aditya (product/legal ops) to provide artifacts and confirm DocuSign routing.

Short answers:  
- Key custody: Redwood-managed by default for Hosted; Dedicated and Private can be BYOK (customer keys in their KMS/HSM). We support HSM-backed keys via KMS integration and can add explicit language to the TOMs exhibit.
- BYOK handoff: we use an import/unwrap workflow (customer uploads public material & registers key IDs). Rotation: configurable, we recommend 90-day rotation but support 30–365 day cadence. We will document rollback steps in the annex.
- Evidence: attaching a marked-up TOMs with the encryption and key-custody sections highlighted. Also attaching a key inventory template you can preview. DocuSign: we will route the envelope from redwood-legal@redwood.com; envelope status link included when sent.

Next steps I propose:
1) Neha to send a 1–2 page technical annex addressing BYOK/HSM details and the export-control/evidence statements.
2) Aditya to prepare DocuSign envelope and confirm signer list and eID requirements.
3) I’ll review AtlasFin markup and triage any redlines for Legal.

If that works I’ll aim to turn around the annex by EOD tomorrow (10/06).

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Markus Lind <markus.lind@atlasfin.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-06T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA: TOMs — cryptography questions and signing plan

Markus / Chloe — attaching the technical annex (see attachment: Redwood_TOMs_v3_marked.pdf) and a key inventory CSV template (key_inventory_2027Q3.csv). Highlights from the annex below.

--- Annex highlights ---
- Deployment modes: hosted (Redwood-managed keys), dedicated/private (BYOK supported).
- HSM support: we integrate with cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) and support keys with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 where the cloud provider offers it. For on-prem/private we support KMIP compatible HSMs.
- Key import/registration: customer uploads a public-wrapped key via our secure import API; Redwood records key ID and enforces usage policies via our KMS abstraction. We do not persist unencrypted private key material.
- Rotation & revocation: rotation policy configurable; we recommend 90 days. Revocation requires an administrative request plus verification via registered admin identity; we include a rollback plan in Appendix B.
- Evidence artifacts provided: TLS configuration snapshot (ciphers: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384), S3 bucket policy template for EU residency, and our Data Flow diagram for signing workflow.
- Signing metadata: DocuSign envelope metadata is retained as audit records; the signing process does route through DocuSign but payloads can be proxied to keep signing endpoints in EU if required (we can arrange EU-hosted DocuSign tenant on request).

Please review the attached annex and call out any sections you want tightened into the DPA language.

-Neha
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_TOMs_v3_marked.pdf; key_inventory_2027Q3.csv

From: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@atlasfin.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Lind <markus.lind@atlasfin.com>
Date: 2027-10-06T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: TOMs — cryptography questions and signing plan

Neha — thank you for the annex, that helps. A couple of legal/contract items:  

- We need explicit DPA language that customer-supplied keys are "customer property" and Redwood warrants not to export key material without explicit instruction.
- Please add wording that audit logs for key usage will be retained for at least 2 years and available on request under NDA.
- For BYOK, we want a clause requiring Redwood to notify AtlasFin within 24 hours of any key compromise, with remediation timelines.

We’ll produce a marked DPA with those redlines and circulate. Also, please confirm whether the DocuSign envelope will include the TOMs exhibit as a separate PDF attachment (preferred) or inline.

Best,
Ella
Senior Counsel, AtlasFin

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@atlasfin.com>, chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Lind <markus.lind@atlasfin.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA: TOMs — cryptography questions and signing plan

Ella — thanks for the redlines. Quick operational notes:  
- We will add express language in the DPA: "Customer keys remain Customer property; Redwood will not export or persist private key material."
- Audit logs: we can commit to 2-year retention for key usage logs; delivery mechanism will be a secure S3 presigned export or syslog transfer under NDA.
- Key compromise notice: we can commit to 24-hour notification and an initial incident report within 72 hours; remediation timelines to be agreed but we propose 14 business days for containment and 30 business days for remediation plan.
- DocuSign packaging: we will include the TOMs exhibit as a separate PDF attachment in the envelope and send the envelope from redwood-legal@redwood.com. CC: redwood-secops@redwood.com for audit trail.

I’ll prepare the envelope and trigger DocuSign today; the envelope id will be shared once created. If those operational timelines look good to AtlasFin we can update the DPA with final language and route for signature.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: docusign-envelope-987654.pdf (stub — envelope draft)

From: Markus Lind <markus.lind@atlasfin.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ella Rodriguez <ella.rodriguez@atlasfin.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: TOMs — cryptography questions and signing plan

Aditya/Chloe/Neha — that all sounds reasonable. Please proceed to update the DPA language with the three committed points (customer property of keys; 2-year audit retention; 24-hour compromise notice + timelines). Once we have the updated DPA and the DocuSign envelope link we will get Legal to sign on our side.

One last ask: please include a short sentence in the DPA that if AtlasFin requires EU-only processing for signing metadata, Redwood will use EU-hosted signing proxies where available. That will close our compliance review.

Thanks — look forward to the envelope.

-Markus
Head of InfoSec, AtlasFin
